Figure 2: Overview of the proposed clustering-enhanced domain adaptation framework for cross-domain intrusion detection in industrial control systems. The left part illustrates the challenge of domain shift and unknown attacks in dynamic industrial environments. The middle part presents the proposed method, which combines PCA-based feature homogenization, K-Medoids-guided structural correspondence estimation, and spectral-transform-based feature alignment. The right part summarizes the effectiveness of the proposed framework in improving unknown attack detection accuracy, F-score, and stability over baseline methods.

Figure 5: Visual comparison of the proposed framework and baseline models on four cross-domain unknown attack detection tasks. The upper panel reports the accuracy results, while the lower panel presents the F-score results. The proposed method consistently achieves the best performance across different transfer settings, demonstrating its superiority in both classification correctness and class-balanced detection effectiveness.
